long_description: An MCP server for the Cloudinary Video API. Broadcast live streams over RTMP with HLS delivery, archiving, and simulcast to YouTube or Facebook. Generate videos from images and a prompt with Image to Video (Beta, add-on). Get timestamped visual transcripts of stored videos with AI Video Analysis (Beta). Build Video Canvas applets: node-based transformation pipelines saved as named transformations.
name: @cloudinary/video-mcp

tools.name: list-canvas-applets
tools.description:
List applets

Returns the account's saved Video Canvas applets as summaries, without their inputs, blocks, connections, or outputs.

tools.name: create-canvas-applet
tools.description:
Create an applet

Creates an applet from its content (inputs, blocks, connections, and outputs). Cloudinary compiles the action blocks to validate them and returns the stored applet. For a derived applet, the compiled blocks are also saved as a named transformation.

tools.name: get-canvas-applet
tools.description:
Get an applet

Returns a single applet with its full content, including its inputs, blocks, connections, and outputs.

tools.name: replace-canvas-applet
tools.description:
Replace an applet's content

Replaces the full content of an existing applet and recompiles its action blocks to validate them. For a derived applet, its backing named transformation is also updated.

tools.name: delete-canvas-applet
tools.description:
Delete an applet

Deletes an applet and its stored content. For a derived applet, the named transformation that backs it isn't deleted, so delivery URLs and SDK calls that reference it keep working. To stop delivering the transformation, delete the named transformation separately.

tools.name: get-live-stream-stats
tools.description:
Get live stream input stats

Returns the input stats collected for a live stream during a time range, such as the incoming video and audio bitrates, the resolution and codecs declared by the streaming software, and the number of dropped frames. Stats are kept for 30 days. Returns an empty list when no stats were collected in the time range, for example when the stream wasn't receiving input.

tools.name: get-live-stream-health
tools.description:
Get live stream health

Assesses the health of a live stream's input from the stats collected during a time range. The assessment compares the incoming video and audio bitrates to the bitrates expected for the stream's resolution, frame rate, and codecs, and also takes into account the ratio of incoming to outgoing bitrate and the number of dropped frames. By default, it covers the last 15 seconds, so you can poll it to monitor a stream while it runs.

tools.name: get-live-stream-viewer-metrics
tools.description:
Get live stream viewer metrics

Returns viewer metrics for the latest session of a live stream: how many people are watching now, how many watched in total, and the average watch time. A session runs from when the stream is activated until it goes idle.

Viewer data is reported by the Cloudinary Video Player, which sends an event when a viewer starts and stops watching the stream, unless the player's `cloudinaryAnalytics` option is set to `false`. Viewers who watch the stream in other players aren't counted.

tools.name: get-live-stream-viewer-time-series
tools.description:
Get live stream viewer metrics over time

Returns one viewer metric for the latest session of a live stream as a time series, with a data point every five seconds from `from` to `to`. Use it to chart how the audience changed during the session. Viewer data comes from the Cloudinary Video Player, as described for the viewer metrics endpoint.

tools.name: generate-video-from-image
tools.description:
Create a video generation job

Submits an image and prompt for video generation and returns a job you can poll for the result.

tools.name: get-video-generation-job
tools.description:
Poll a video generation job

Returns the current status of a generation job. When the status is `completed`, the response includes the generated video's asset details and delivery URL.

tools.name: list-image-to-video-prompts

Create an image to video prompt

tools.name: analyze-video
tools.description:
Create an AI Video Analysis job

Submits a stored video asset for visual analysis and returns a job you can poll for the result.

tools.name: get-video-analysis-job

Poll an AI Video Analysis job

Returns the current status of an analysis job. When the status is `completed`, the response includes the generated visual transcript file's asset details and delivery URL.

tools.name: list-video-elements
tools.description:
List a video's elements

Returns the elements of the given type that are attached to a video, such as its custom poster or its transcript files. Each element is a separate asset related to the video. Results are paginated; when `next_cursor` is returned, pass it as `cursor` to get the next page.

tools.name: upload-video-element
tools.description:
Upload a video element

Uploads a file as a video element and attaches it to the video whose asset ID you pass as `videoAssetId` in the path. The element is stored as its own asset, in the same asset folder as the video, with a public ID based on the video's public ID.

How to send the file depends on the element type:
- `poster`: send the image as `file` in a `multipart/form-data` request, or send `{"url": "<image URL>"}` as `application/json` to upload it from a URL. The poster's public ID is `<video public ID>_poster`.
- `transcript`: send a `.srt`, `.vtt`, or `.transcript` file as `file` in a `multipart/form-data` request. Cloudinary converts it to its `.transcript` format. To upload a translation, also send `language_code`. The public ID is `<video public ID>.<language_code>.transcript`, or `<video public ID>.transcript` without a language code.
- `visual_transcript`: send a `.srt`, `.vtt`, or `.transcript` file as `file` in a `multipart/form-data` request. Cloudinary converts it to its `.transcript` format. The public ID is `<video public ID>.visual.transcript`.

Files can be up to 30 MB. Chapters can't be uploaded.

tools.name: delete-video-elements
tools.description:
Delete video elements

Deletes elements of the given type from a video. By default, deletes all of the video's elements of that type, for example every transcript including translations. To delete a single element, pass its `assetId`. The element assets are deleted, not just detached from the video. The response confirms the request but doesn't list the deleted elements, so to check what's left, list the video's elements.
